messages.author: d606027d19014b7f
messages.subject: Question about landmark number limitation
parts:
Hi all,

I have three specimens with a large dataset of 3D landmarks (11,000 per specimen). Some landmarks are missing and I therefore need to estimate their position using estimate.missing before being able to perform a GPA with gpagen. It appears that there is a limitation of around 579 Landmarks. When I reduce the 3D array to 579 landmarks [1:579, 1:3, 1:3] I receive an output, but as soon as I increase the number of Landmarks above the 579 threshold, e.g.  [1:580, 1:3, 1:3], I receive the following error: 

Error in gpagen(A[, , -spec.NA, PrinAxes = FALSE) :
  Coordinates array does not have proper dimensions

Is there a way to circumvent this limitation? Subdividing the specimens into smaller junks of 579 landmarks might skew the GPA and is thus not really an option.

I would be grateful for any help with my issue.

Many thanks in advance,

Ashleigh

messages.author: fbfd20ce829c6c6c
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Question about landmark number limitation
parts:
Hi Ashleigh, 

It seems what is triggering this is the following from gpagen:

"if (length(dim(A)) != 3)
            stop("Coordinates array does not have proper dimensions")".

Thus, have you checked to confirm that you are supplying an array with dimensions = 3?
My guess is that "A[, , -spec.NA]" produces an error since you are removing part of the landmarks in only one dimension, rather than removing specimens with missing landmarks in this line of code (I assume that was your intention). Would "A[-spec.NA, , ]" work?

Best, 
Bryan Juarez

Hi Ashleigh,

I’m wondering if your exact input was gpagen(A[, , -spec.NA, PrinAxes = FALSE)  (as it appears in the error), in which case you’re missing a closing bracket for A.

Otherwise, I was unable to reproduce such an error with sample data stacked up past 580 landmarks. Thus, it would be helpful to diagnose the issue if you provide a script and data that produces the error in question. 

Thanks,
Erica
